name: POST /api/leadflow/sla/tick - advance the T+0 to T+45 escalation ladder
description:
Fires every rung that has come due, to the audience SOP §04 and §05 name for it: T+0 assign and write NEXT, T+1 acknowledgement, T+5 unaccepted reminder with the backup notified, T+15 rep reminder plus yellow manager warning, T+25 red alert with the optional P1 freeze, T+30 BREACH, T+45 critical incident (a9c60302-b7ba-4eab-bfe5-cf68d479d1d4#AC1).

A DUPLICATED TICK NEVER DOUBLE-ALERTS (a9c60302-b7ba-4eab-bfe5-cf68d479d1d4#AC2), and that is a uniqueness problem rather than a scheduling one. Ticks arrive from the timer, from a webhook and from an operator; two landing on the same lead a millisecond apart both read "T+15 has not fired" and both send. So a rung is claimed by INSERTING into leadflow_escalation_fire, which carries UNIQUE (lead_id, rung) - the second insert is refused by the database and a refused insert means somebody else already alerted. No read-then-write, no lock, no window. MEASURED LIVE: two consecutive ticks on one lead returned fired [0] suppressed [] and then fired [] suppressed [0].

SUPPRESSED IS REPORTED, NOT DISCARDED. A healthy re-tick has to be distinguishable from a ladder that has stopped firing, and only the suppressed count does that.

EVERY DUE RUNG FIRES, NOT JUST THE LATEST. A tick delayed by an outage must not skip T+5 and T+15 on its way to T+25, because the backup was never told and the manager never saw the warning. Each rung is claimed separately, so a catch-up sweep sends what was genuinely missed and suppresses what was not.

ONE INCIDENT PER SWEEP AT T+45, listing every affected lead (a9c60302-b7ba-4eab-bfe5-cf68d479d1d4#AC4). Forty leads breaching because one workflow broke is one incident with forty rows; forty incidents is a pager nobody can act on. The idempotency key is bucketed by hour so a retry inside the sweep window joins the existing incident rather than opening a second.

MEASURED FROM THE ORIGINAL SOURCE TIMESTAMP so a reassigned lead does not restart its ladder. QA: depends on register and login.

testCases.name: A sweep reports what fired and what the constraint suppressed
Re-running the sweep fires nothing it has already fired
NEGATIVE: ticking an unknown lead reports that nothing was advanced
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.when: a lead_id is supplied that does not exist. Deliberately not a silent no-op: a caller ticking a lead by id expects to hear that the id was wrong rather than that nothing was due.

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer.

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify.
